To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

persistent DNA damage signalling is required for senescence associated cytokine secretion and that this pathway is required for senescent cells, which have a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment, to communicate their compromised states to the surrounding tissue.
DNA damage signalling, but not cell cycle arrest, triggers senescent cells, including oncogene induced senescent cells and cells that bypass senesence, to secrete inflammatory cytokines.
Persistent DNA damage signalling triggers senescence-associated inflammatory cytokine secretion, which is required for the senescent cells' ability to promote cancer progression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of DNA damage induced senescence, and its consequences for cancer.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the secretion of inflammatory cytokine from senescent cells.
the mechanisms that control the cell cycle and the mechanisms by which cells respond to DNA damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
persistent DNA damage signals trigger a senescence associated cytokine secretion program that is essential to maintain a tissue microenvironment that is permissive to cancer suppression.
the DNA damage response (DDR) is a new and important pathway that allows damaged cells to signal their compromised state to surrounding tissue, thus initiating an inflammatory response.
the DDR is a key regulator of senescence associated inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
persistent DNA damage signaling is required for senescence associated cytokine secretion.
persistent DNA damage signalling is required for the senescence associated secretion of inflammatory cytokine.
the DDR proteins ATM and NBS1, but not p53 and pRB, initiate and maintain senescent cells' ability to signal their compromised state to surrounding tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA damage signaling, which is normally associated with cell cycle arrest and DNA repair, also drives senescence-associated inflammatory cytokine secretion in human cells.
senescent cells are not just bystanders in tissue aging and cancer.

DNA damage responses can be divided into transient DNA damage responses, which are associated with repair, and persistent DNA damage signaling, which is not associated with repair, but is instead associated with cell cycle arrest, senescence, and the secretion of cytokines.
